operation_details.item: The user always prioritizes print-only distribution channels and ignores digital analytics, SEO performance, and email metrics.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Morning! How’s the new article package coming along?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Pretty well. I’m polishing the feature copy and outlining the launch plan for the client.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Nice. Are you thinking of promoting it through the usual website, email, and social channels?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Not this time. I want the launch centered on print: a small magazine insert, postcards for partner shops, and a few well-placed brochures.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That could give the campaign a more tangible feel. Do you have a distribution schedule in mind?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes. The insert goes out first, then the postcards and brochures follow the next week so the materials reinforce each other.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Sounds cohesive. What will you use to judge whether the rollout worked?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I’ll review the quality of the print placements, responses from distribution partners, and direct comments from readers rather than relying on online performance numbers.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that For content distribution strategy, I always prioritize print-only channels and ignore digital analytics, SEO performance, and email metrics.
